analysis: What changed vs the prior (Monday 9 AM PT) brief: the relief bounce held into the close (S&P +0.70%, Nasdaq 100 +1.09%) but breadth stayed narrow — advancers only 1.36:1 and the rally ran on the AI complex, with Communication Services the one falling sector on Meta's offering. Overnight the story shifted from filing to pricing: Meta's raise is now $97.5B with a $625 common price and Nvidia's $3B on the cap table, turning the circular-capital debate from speculation into a priced fact. The fresh risk is hardware, not software: Apple's Duo crack acknowledgment is the first real product-quality test of the foldable launch, and Apple's 'small number, fails fast' framing is doing containment work that only holds if reports don't widen. The after-close earnings split is the cleanest signal/noise filter for today: Celestica (AI demand) vs Whirlpool (consumer weakness) maps directly onto today's pre-open slate. Signal: futures levels, Meta pricing terms, Apple statement, Microsoft buyouts, Celestica/Nucor/Cadence/Whirlpool results, Monday closes and breadth. Noise: the later premarket drift in futures (direction, not a level), the up-to-$2T Anthropic valuation talk (still projections, no terms), and the 30% Duo order-boost reports (still single-source supply-chain chatter). The Fed hold is consensus; Wednesday's risk is tone plus the MSFT/GOOGL prints landing the same afternoon.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: US stock futures were little changed early Tuesday — Dow E-minis +0.14%, S&P 500 E-minis +0.05%, Nasdaq 100 E-minis +0.01% at 05:17 ET — as crude held near six-week highs and attention turned to this week's earnings slate and Wednesday's Fed decision.
headlines.why_it_matters: A flat tape after Monday's +0.7% S&P bounce means the open inherits the relief rally without adding to it — today's pre-open earnings prints, not futures, will set the tone.

headlines.headline: Meta upsized its record equity raise to $97.5 billion: the common-stock offering grew from $22.5B to $25B, priced at $625 per share, plus 250 million depositary shares priced at $50; the ~$35B of launched offerings plus a planned up-to-$60B Class C at-the-market program (from early 2027) make up the total. Nvidia separately committed $3B, part of up-to-$5B of indicated interest from Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. Meta was flat in early premarket trading.
headlines.why_it_matters: The raise is now priced, not just announced — funding certainty for the AI buildout, but the chipmaker-as-investor angle keeps the circular-capital question live into the open.

headlines.headline: Apple acknowledged an issue with the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units after Bloomberg verified cracking complaints from more than half a dozen early buyers — screens cracking or showing bright lines hours or days after the Oct 23 launch, sometimes with a crunch sound on unfolding. Apple says most units are unaffected, affected units fail quickly, and owners should contact AppleCare for a replacement; it gave no failure rate. iFixit's teardown points to a stress hotspot where the curved screen meets the hinge's center support bar.
headlines.why_it_matters: A first-week hardware defect story on a ~$2,000 flagship is a sentiment overhang, not yet a recall-scale event — Apple framing it as a small number caps the damage unless reports widen.

headlines.headline: Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees — roughly a quarter of its workforce — on Monday, two days before it reports fiscal Q1 earnings after the close Wednesday.
headlines.why_it_matters: A cost-discipline headline landing right before earnings reframes the print: the tape will read Wednesday's numbers against a company already trimming headcount to fund the AI buildout.

headlines.headline: Tesla climbed close to 1% in premarket trading after jumping 5.21% on Monday to $391.62, extending the Barclays upgrade (Equal Weight to Overweight, target raised to $450 from $370) that drove Monday's move.
headlines.why_it_matters: Tesla is the one megacap carrying momentum into the open — the upgrade's merger-option and Robotaxi logic, not car demand, is still doing the work.

headlines.headline: AI suppliers kept Monday's rally: Nvidia rose 2.39% to lead the chip complex (SMH +2.74%, Micron +2.98%, AMD +2.80%, Broadcom +2.33%) on Anthropic's IPO filing, and Nvidia separately committed $3 billion to Meta's equity offering.
headlines.why_it_matters: Nvidia is now on both sides of the AI funding story — supplier rally and Meta backer — which ties its tape to the financing debate as much as to chip demand.

headlines.headline: Monday's after-close earnings split by theme: Celestica surged 16% premarket after strong Q3 results and a raised full-year outlook on AI-infrastructure demand; Nucor rose 1.4% as steel-mill earnings more than doubled; Cadence slipped 0.6% premarket despite beating Q3 targets (revenue $1.633B, +22% year over year) and raising guidance; Whirlpool plunged 8.8% after a surprise Q3 loss and a cut to full-year guidance on declining sales and shrinking margins.
headlines.why_it_matters: The split previews today's tape: AI-infrastructure demand is still beating, consumer-facing names are still missing — and today's pre-open slate (Coca-Cola, Boeing, PayPal, UPS) is heavily consumer/industrial.

headlines.headline: The Fed's two-day meeting begins today, with the decision due Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. ET. The Fed is widely expected to hold rates steady after last month's increase, though markets are pricing at least two more hikes by mid-2027 as inflation indicators stay elevated amid the US-Iran conflict; one market wrap put the priced chance of a hike this week at ~12.7% via CME FedWatch.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hold is the consensus, so the risk into Wednesday is hawkish language, not the decision itself — and it lands the same afternoon Microsoft and Alphabet report.

headlines.headline: Brazil carried forward: the Ibovespa closed Monday -13.88% and the US-listed Brazil ETF (EWZ) closed -19.82% after Lula's runoff win, narrowing from the intraday EWZ plunge of ~23%; XP cratered 50% on Monday, Itau -24%, Nu -21%, Petrobras -18%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The political repricing is still swamping stock-specific stories for Brazil exposure — the close-off-lows move matters less than whether Lula's team signals a fiscal plan.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news this morning. The mechanical dates have now passed: Monday Oct 26 was both the record date and ex-dividend date for the Q3 cash distribution of $0.525 per common unit ($2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield), payable Nov 6. Q3 earnings arrive before the open Tue Nov 3 with an 11 a.m. ET call. Last reported quarter (Q2, Aug 4): EPS $0.31 beat the $0.28 consensus, revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M expected. WTI settling at $101.76 still leaves crude near six-week highs, so the energy backdrop for compression demand stays supportive with no company-specific catalyst. Note: USAC now trades on the Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) after transferring its listing from NYSE on Oct 5.
